newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Dixons sees growth in spending.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Dixons sees growth in spending.

text.p: British electronics and computer retailer Dixons Group Plc is seeing growth in consumer spending but no boom, managing director John Clare said in an interview.
"There isn't a big consumer boom but there is growth in the consumer economy," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Clare added that "if (the economy) is managed well, we can't see any reason why it should not continue."
Dixons saw sales from existing stores rise eight percent in the first eight weeks of the second half after a similar increase in the first half.
It said in a statement that pre-tax profits for the first half jumped 53 percent to 57.5 million stg and paid out a dividend of 2.4 pence, up from 2.05 pence.
Clare, who said the sales rise was in line with the company's expectations, said Dixons had seen "a distinct pick up in our markets since March or April" of 1996.
"The available money is a little bit more than last year," he added, but consumers were "more discerning, more choosy."
Personal computers and accessories including software accounted for around 26 percent of sales in the first half, Clare said, inching nearer 30 percent over Christmas.

"I expect personal computer sales to continue to grow...household penetration is still very low in the UK," he said, adding that PC sales would "continue to be very important and probably continue to grow."

He said margins, at similar levels to last year in the first eight weeks of the second half, were hard to predict with a "swings and roundabouts" pull between lower margins on PC hardware and benefits of reduced credit promotion activity.
"There are two contrary forces at work...PCs are taking a higher share of the product mix...(but) there are benefits from reduced competitive activity, particularly in credit promotions," he said.
Retail outlets of regional electricity companies (Recs) have been trimmed, for example, as a result of takeovers and consolidation in the sector.

Dixons opens around ten PC World out-of-town PC superstores each year, Clare said, and "we expect that expansion rate to continue," along with some 20 Currys domestic electrical superstores, half of which will be resites of existing outlets.
Clare said digital technology was likely to be another growth market for the company with wide-screen digital television likely to debut in 1998.
"Digital technology is generally coming in in a big way...(but) I don't think it will replace PCs, because PCs will continue to grow," Clare said.
Dixons already retails digital cameras, digital audio equipment and digital camcorders as part of its digital product range.

He said the group would be assessing the impact of government plans to raise Insurance Premium Tax to 17.5 percent from a previous 2.5 percent which would cover extended warranties on consumer electrical products. -- Jo Winterbottom, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
